start_walkthrough.title: Start walkthrough
start_walkthrough.description: Create a narrated walkthrough and get its handle and link. The reply is deliberately short: call add_slides at once with only the opening, the title slide plus one or two short spoken sentences. The add_slides description has the format essentials; the full guide comes with the first playable reply.

args.title: Walkthrough title, shown on the title slide and in the player.
args.frame: Slide shape: landscape (default, 1280×720), square (960×960) or portrait (720×1280, for phones).
args.voice: English Kokoro voice id. Omit for the default. Voices:
args.speed: Speech rate from 0.8 to 1.3; 1.0 is normal.
args.project_dir: Absolute path of the project. Code blocks with file= and image paths are read from it and must stay inside it. Defaults to the client's root, then the server's working directory.

add_slides.title: Add slides
add_slides.description:
Append slides to a walkthrough, written in Markdown.

Calls:
- First call: only the title slide and one or two short spoken sentences. It returns when the link is playable, with the full guide. Send the link to the user then, before anything else.
- Every later call: one to three whole slides. Never resend earlier Markdown. Never split a slide or its code block across calls.
- Replies list problems: fix them in later slides, or replace a broken slide with revise_slide.

Format:
- Slide: each #, ## or ### heading starts one. Optional attributes: `## Title {#id .build}`; .build reveals parts as cues reach them.
- Narration: plain paragraphs are spoken, each voiced separately. Put identifiers in `backticks`; `[text]{say="spoken"}` fixes pronunciation.
- Shown text: `>` lines are shown, never spoken; under the first heading, one is the subtitle.
- Visual: at most one per slide: fenced code, diff, ```mermaid diagram, ```math formula, pipe table, list, or image ![alt](path).
- Code from disk, with an empty body and the file's own line numbers in the gutter:
```python file=src/app.py lines=10-24
```
  Inline code may set start=10.
- Diff: ```python old then ```python new blocks; ```diff with -/+ lines, one hunk per slide; or ```diff file=path rev=A (against the working tree) or rev=A..B.
- List: `- **Title**: text {#id}`; without {#id}, the id is the title, lowercased and hyphenated. `1.` items are steps; .cards on the heading shows cards.
- Cues are links in narration. The pointer moves when the label's first word is spoken, within the current slide only.
  [label](#L12) line 12 | #L12-18 a range | [label](#L12 "exact text") only that text on line 12 | #-L5 old side, #+L7 new side of a diff | #id a list item, card or Mermaid node | #row-2 the second table row, or a {#id} ending its last cell | # the whole visual; [label](# "text") finds that text in it.

Opening example:
# How the retry loop works
> Backoff in the HTTP client

A failed request can be sent up to four times. We'll follow one through the client.

args.markdown: Slides in Markdown. First call: only the title slide and one or two spoken sentences. Later calls: one to three whole slides, nothing already sent.

revise_slide.title: Revise slide
revise_slide.description: Replace one slide, found by its id, with new Markdown. Only narration whose text changed is voiced again; the rest keeps its audio. Omit the heading to keep the slide's title, classes and attributes. Use it for a slide a reply reported as broken, or to rework a finished walkthrough: find its handle with list_walkthroughs and read its Markdown from the resource showntell://walkthroughs/{id}.

args.slide: Id of the slide to replace: its {#id}, or the id generated from its title as named in replies.
args.markdown: The complete new slide: heading (optional), visual, shown text and narration. One slide only.

finish_walkthrough.title: Finish walkthrough
finish_walkthrough.description: Close the walkthrough after its last slide. Records the end questions and returns a summary with any remaining problems. Then tell the user it is finished and give the link.

args.questions: Two or three short follow-up questions the viewer might ask next, as a list of strings. Offered at the end of the walkthrough. Optional when the Markdown already lists them under a `.questions` heading; questions passed here replace those.

list_walkthroughs.title: List walkthroughs
list_walkthroughs.description: List recent walkthroughs with their handles, titles and links. Use it to find the handle of a walkthrough to revise later, including one from an earlier session. Its Markdown source is the resource showntell://walkthroughs/{id}, where id is the part of the handle before the dot.
